name: Latchkey — The 2040s Collapse Revival Scene
description: Where Twenty-Twentiers romanticize the pre-Collapse chaos, Latchkey specifically fetishizes the decade immediately following — the 2040s reconstruction era, with its jury-rigged infrastructure, early BCI mass-adoption aesthetics, and the specific visual language of emergency civic signage that blanketed cities during the Reorganization. Members collect physical 2040s reconstruction-era objects: emergency shelter kits, early-gen BCI headbands worn externally, hand-painted municipal notices, and the distinctive high-vis orange and matte grey color palette of the period. Their music is called 'rebuild' — a genre built on looped emergency broadcast tones, early synthetic speech artifacts, and hand-percussion. Latchkey skews older than most retro scenes, attracting Tier 2-3 adults in their 30s-40s whose parents or grandparents actually lived through the Reorganization.
cultural_impact: Latchkey's obsession with the Reorganization era has accidentally produced some of the most rigorous grassroots historical documentation of the 2040s in the Great Lakes corridor — their object collections and oral history archives are more complete than any corporate-sponsored museum exhibit. Several academic historians now quietly consult with Latchkey curators.
locations: The Shelter — a Latchkey venue built inside a genuine 2041 emergency hab module, North Side
Salvage Archive Row, Tier 2 warehouse district
Rebuild Night at the Caldwell Plate — monthly event
story_hooks: A Latchkey archivist discovers a sealed 2041 emergency shelter that contains evidence of a corporate atrocity during the Reorganization — and a corponation will do anything to keep it buried.
The 'rebuild' music genre is suddenly being sampled without credit in a major corporate entertainment product, and the Latchkey community is too fragmented to mount a coordinated response.
An actual 2040s survivor — now elderly — begins attending Latchkey events and is disturbed by how the scene romanticizes what she experienced as catastrophe.
